title: Multistage development of short-range spin correlations and weak magnetic order in the two coupled trillium lattices of K2Fe2(MoO4)(PO4)2
authors: J. Khatua, Sritharan Krishnamoorthi, Changhyun Koo, Gyungbin Ban, Taeyun Kim, Yugo Oshima, Marc Uhlarz, John Wilkinson, Peter J. Baker, Kyeong Jun Lee, Mani Shankar, Seo Hyoung Chang, R. Sankar, Kwang-Yong Choi
abstract: Trillium lattices, where magnetic ions form a chiral network of corner-sharing triangles, offer a three-dimensional magnetic framework that can host fragile classical spin-liquid states. Herein, we report on the magnetization, specific heat, electron spin resonance (ESR), and muon spin relaxation ($μ$SR) of K$_{2}$Fe$_{2}$(MoO$_{4}$)(PO$_{4}$)$_{2}$ single crystals. Magnetization measurements reveal strong antiferromagnetic interactions coexisting with weak magnetic order at $T_{\rm N} = 5.2$~K, as evidenced by a $λ$-like anomaly observed in the magnetic susceptibility, a critical enhancement of the muon spin relaxation rate and the wipeout of the ESR signal as the temperature approaches $T_{\rm N}$. Above $T_{\rm N}$, two distinct developments of short-range spin correlations are identified at $T_{\rm H} = 34$~K and $T_{\rm L} = 10$~K, supported by magnetic specific heat anomalies and the temperature dependence of the ESR linewidth and $g$-factor. Upon cooling below $T_{\rm N}$, an anomaly appears at $T^{*} = 3.2$~K in thermodynamic observables and the muon spin relaxation rate, indicative of spin reorientation driven by residual interactions. Despite the presence of magnetic order, $μ$SR experiments reveal dynamically fluctuating spins persisting even in the ordered state. Moreover, the suppression of $T_{\rm N}$ under applied magnetic fields ($μ_{0}H \geq 2$~T) suggests that K$_{2}$Fe$_{2}$(MoO$_{4}$)(PO$_{4}$)$_{2}$ constitutes a promising candidate for exploring field-induced spin-liquid behavior in three-dimensionally coupled trillium lattices.
summary: This work experimentally characterizes the magnetic behavior of $	ext{K}_2	ext{Fe}_2(	ext{MoO}_4)(	ext{PO}_4)_2$, a material built from coupled trillium lattices. Measurements reveal multiple distinct temperature scales marking the development of short-range spin correlations, culminating in weak antiferromagnetic order. The results suggest this system is an excellent platform for studying field-induced quantum spin liquid behavior.
main_problem: The study investigates the development of short-range spin correlations and weak magnetic order within a specific, geometrically frustrated magnetic material.
main_result: The material exhibits multiple distinct temperature scales for correlation development ($T_H=34	ext{ K}, T_L=10	ext{ K}$) followed by weak long-range antiferromagnetic ordering at $T_N=5.2	ext{ K}$, suggesting complex magnetic interactions.
method: The research employed a combination of bulk measurements, including magnetization, specific heat, Electron Spin Resonance (ESR), and Muon Spin Relaxation ($\mu$SR).
model_or_system: The physical system is the single crystal $	ext{K}_2	ext{Fe}_2(	ext{MoO}_4)(	ext{PO}_4)_2$, which features two coupled trillium lattices of magnetic $	ext{Fe}^{3+}$ ions, forming a complex, frustrated 3D magnetic network.
key_observables: Magnetic susceptibility ($\chi(T)$), specific heat anomalies ($\lambda$-like), muon spin relaxation rate enhancement, and ESR signal changes.
important_parameters: $T_N = 5.2	ext{ K}$ (Néel temperature), $T_H = 34	ext{ K}$, $T_L = 10	ext{ K}$, and applied magnetic fields ($\mu_0H \geq 2	ext{ T}$).
main_assumptions: The weak magnetic order is attributed to residual interactions atop dominant Heisenberg exchange, and the system shows signs of field-induced spin-liquid behavior.
figures_summary: Figures detail crystal structure analysis (XRD) confirming phase purity and lattice details, alongside measurements showing temperature dependence of susceptibility and anomalies related to spin correlations and ordering.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first establishing the structural framework using XRD, then characterizing the magnetic interactions via $\chi(T)$ and specific heat to identify multiple correlation temperatures ($T_H, T_L$), followed by detailed probes ($\mu$SR) confirming dynamic fluctuations even in the ordered state.
why_interesting: The study provides experimental evidence of hierarchical spin correlations across multiple energy scales in a geometrically frustrated lattice, which is highly relevant for understanding complex many-body ground states beyond simple mean-field theories.
